samples: This pure, side-effect-free module models invoices as a customer plus a list of lines (each with a description, a quantity of at least 1, and a non-negative unit price) and a discount percentage limited to 0–100. It computes each line's total, the subtotal of all lines, and a final total with the percentage discount taken off and rounded to two decimal places, using exact Decimal arithmetic rather than floats. It does not handle taxes, currencies, or output formatting, and its tests only cover a 10% discount case and an empty invoice, so check the rounding behavior against your own rules (for example, how halves round) before relying on it.

This module models an invoice as a customer plus lines (each with a quantity of at least 1 and a non-negative unit price) and a discount percentage that must be between 0 and 100. It computes each line's total, the invoice subtotal, and a final total with the discount taken off and the result rounded to two decimal places. It uses exact Decimal arithmetic, needs no outside access such as files or network, and ships with tests covering a 10% discount and an empty invoice, though the program doesn't say which rounding rule applies to half-cent cases, so check that if it matters to you.

This program computes invoice amounts: each line is priced as quantity times unit price, the lines are summed into a subtotal, and a percentage discount (0 to 100) is subtracted, with the final total rounded to two decimal places. It uses exact Decimal arithmetic rather than floating point, and it rejects invalid data such as quantities below 1, negative prices, or discounts outside 0 to 100. It is pure (no I/O or other capabilities needed) and includes tests for a 10% discount and for an empty invoice, though it handles only a single percentage discount and no taxes or currencies.

This program defines invoices made of billable lines (each with a quantity of at least 1 and a non-negative unit price) and a customer-wide discount percentage restricted to 0–100. It computes each line's total, the invoice subtotal, and a final total that applies the percentage discount and rounds to two decimal places, using exact decimal arithmetic rather than floating point. It is pure (no I/O or other capabilities needed), and includes tests covering a 10% discount and an empty invoice, so it suits anyone who wants a simple, self-contained invoice calculator, though it handles only a single percentage discount and no taxes or currencies.

This program computes invoice amounts: it defines lines (a quantity of at least 1 and a non-negative unit price) and invoices (a customer, a list of lines, and a discount percentage limited to 0–100). It can give the cost of a single line, the subtotal of all lines, and a final total with the percentage discount taken off and the result rounded to two decimal places. It uses exact decimal arithmetic, performs no input/output or network access, and has tests covering a 10% discount and an empty invoice, so it looks safe to use for straightforward discount billing, though it does not handle taxes or multiple currencies.
